items.back: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], s = (a+b+c)/2. (sides 13, 14, 15 give s = 21 and area = 84.) No extra ½.

items.front: Circle area, circumference, sector area, ring area?
items.back: A=πr², C=2πr; sector=(θ/360)πr², arc=(θ/360)2πr; ring=π(R²−r²). Use π=22/7 when r is a multiple of 7.

items.front: Equilateral triangle area & height; square/rectangle diagonals?
items.back: Equilateral: area=(√3/4)a², height=(√3/2)a. Square diagonal=a√2; rectangle diagonal=√(l²+b²).

items.examPoint: Right circular cylinder — volume & surface area

items.front: Cone volume, slant height, CSA, TSA?
items.back: V=⅓πr²h; slant l=√(r²+h²); CSA=πrl; TSA=πr(r+l). Don't drop the ⅓.
items.examPoint: Right circular cone — volume, CSA, slant

items.front: Sphere and hemisphere volume & surface area?
items.back: Sphere: V=4/3πr³, SA=4πr². Hemisphere: V=2/3πr³, solid TSA=3πr² (curved 2πr²).

items.front: Cuboid & cube — volume, TSA, space diagonal?
items.back: Cuboid: V=lbh, TSA=2(lb+bh+hl), diagonal=√(l²+b²+h²). Cube: V=a³, TSA=6a², diagonal=a√3.
Volume is conserved: pieces = original volume ÷ one-piece volume. Spheres recast into spheres: count = (R/r)³, not (R/r)².

items.front: Uniform scaling — how do area and volume change with factor k?
items.back: Length ×k, area ×k², volume ×k³. Edge +50% (k=1.5): TSA +125%, volume +237.5%.

items.front: Volume ratio when radius and height ratios differ (cone/cylinder)?
items.back: V ∝ r²h — keep only varying factors. Cones with heights 1:5 and radii 5:3 give (25×1):(9×5) = 25:45 = 5:9.
